verbatim_verdict_text:
## Observations, in order

1. **Website loading and navigation — WEBSITE’s work.**  
   The video opens on a mostly blank D&D Beyond page, followed by the site’s dark navigation bar, promotional banner, and loading spinner. These are not extension features.

2. **Privacy overlay — WEBSITE’s work.**  
   D&D Beyond’s “Your Privacy Choices” cookie dialog appears in the lower-left while the site continues loading. The dimmed page and red “CREATE ACCOUNT” control also belong to the website.

3. **Character sheet loads — WEBSITE’s work.**  
   The Corvo Saggio character sheet appears with its artwork, character data, abilities, hit points, actions, inventory, and other D&D Beyond content. The initial character-sheet layout and content are the website’s product.

4. **Sheet enhancement appears — EXTENSION’s work.**  
   The sheet is subsequently overlaid with red outlines around many sections, decorative framing, and altered section presentation. These outlines and ornamental treatment are visibly distinct from the ordinary D&D Beyond presentation and are attributable to Beyond Print Enhancer.

5. **Extension control panels appear — EXTENSION’s work.**  
   A dark, gold-accented “BEYOND P…” control panel opens on the left. Its visible sections include **LAYOUT** and **OUTPUT**, with controls such as Load, Reset to Default, Manage Clones, Add Shape, Manage Compact, AI Arrange, AI Settings, **PRINT**, Print settings, and Save to Browser.

6. **Layer Management panel appears — EXTENSION’s work.**  
   A separate dark panel opens on the right. It shows **SECTIONS (22)**, a list of sheet boxes, and **SHAPES (1)** with several shape/style thumbnails. Its visual treatment is clearly the extension’s own “codex on the workbench” style rather than D&D Beyond UI.

7. **Initial-state notification — EXTENSION’s work.**  
   A dark toast at the top reads, **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”** This provides feedback that the default template—not a saved layout—is active.

8. **Shape/color interaction — EXTENSION’s work.**  
   The ornamental frame and many section borders change visibly from red to green and later back to a neutral/dark treatment. The corresponding shape thumbnail in Layer Management also appears selected. This demonstrates that shape/style choices can update the enhanced sheet on camera.

9. **No print output or filter verification is shown — absence.**  
   Although the extension’s **PRINT** button and **Print settings** entry are visible, the video never opens a print preview, browser print dialog, or paper/output view. No **CANVAS FILTERS** section, filter slider, Greyscale control, hue control, Apply/Undo operation, or output comparison is sampled.

## Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence

| Suite assertion | Camera status | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| The shipped identity chains are `none`, and the sheet’s own type reaches the paper | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No paper, print preview, rendered output, CSS identity chain, or emitted type is shown on camera. |
| All sliders at their defaults is not neutral and costs colour | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No filter sliders or before/after printed output are shown. The visible red/green sheet changes concern shapes/borders, not the asserted default filter chain. |
| A user’s own setting reaches the paper: Greyscale 0% through the panel’s own slider | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No Greyscale slider or its use is shown, and no paper output is shown. |
| A real hue is emitted again rather than neutralised, and the defaults come back byte-identical | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No emitted hue is sampled, no default restoration is demonstrated, and no byte-identical comparison can be observed visually. |

Although the frames are numerous enough to inspect the interface, they do not sample the behavior covered by this suite. In particular, visual inspection alone cannot establish byte identity.

## Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance

### Basic affordances observed working

- **Distinct extension identity:** The dark floating panels, gold hairlines, typography, and ornament styling are visibly unlike D&D Beyond’s native UI.
- **Layer/section management UI:** Layer Management visibly enumerates 22 sections and provides shape thumbnails and per-section controls.
- **Default-template feedback:** The toast clearly reports that no saved layout exists and the default template is loaded.
- **Visible sheet decoration:** The extension’s red outlines and ornamental frame are clearly visible over the sheet.
- **Shape/style selection feedback:** Selection of a shape/color thumbnail corresponds with a visible red/green/neutral change to the sheet decoration.
- **Print entry points:** **PRINT** and **Print settings** are visibly present and clearly styled as extension controls.

### Missing or rough affordances observed within the demonstrated scope

- The central claimed capability—**canvas/print filter behavior reaching paper**—is not demonstrated at all.
- The **CANVAS FILTERS** controls mentioned in the product scope are not shown open, so Greyscale, hue, defaults, reset, Apply, and Undo cannot be assessed.
- The **PRINT** control is visible but never visibly invoked; there is no print-preview or paper-output state.
- No **loading/transition state** for the extension’s print/filter operation is shown. The only spinner belongs to D&D Beyond’s site loading.
- No extension **error state** is shown.
- No **disabled state** is shown, despite the layer/shape lists containing small action icons whose enabled/disabled behavior is unclear.
- No **toast confirming a filter applied, print started, or undo occurred** is shown; the only toast concerns the missing saved layout.
- No **reset-to-defaults result** is demonstrated.
- No **undo/redo recovery path** is demonstrated.
- The toolbar icon and its **ON badge** are outside the captured area, so activation-state affordances cannot be verified.
- The first-run hint card mentioned in the product scope is not visibly shown; the visible “No saved layout yet…” toast serves a different informational purpose.
- The right panel remains focused on Sections and Shapes during the sampled period; no filter-management state is exposed there.
- A red border is also visible on some underlying sheet areas before the full extension panels appear, making ownership of every red outline visually ambiguous. The later green/neutral changes clearly belong to the extension’s styling, but the full extension styling cannot be separated from website state in every early frame.

Because the asserted print/filter identity and output behavior are never sampled, and several relevant basic states are absent, this video cannot certify the suite’s behavioral contract.

VERDICT: NOT-VISIBLE
